topology: 1 node x 4 A100-SXM4-40GB, 4 MPI ranks with one GPU each, CUDA IPC ring r -> r+1 over NVLink
why: case 23 proves the RECORD; this proves the RESOLUTION. Case 23 runs one process driving four GPUs, so every copy edge it can produce is rank 0 -> rank 0 and it is silent about the chain that turns a device ordinal into an owning rank (_node -> _device_key -> _device_owner). Here four processes each own one GPU and cudaMemcpyPeer round a ring, so the whole matrix is a cross-rank claim. It is also the only case whose entire inter-rank traffic is a copy engine: no kernels, no verbs, no UCX, no NCCL.
why_no_goldens: the ring is fully specified by params — rank r sends iters copies of msg_bytes to rank r+1 mod ranks and nothing else — so every claim is an assertion. A golden would add nothing the assertions do not already state, and would pin ranks and ordinals, which is exactly what the suite's rule forbids.
platform_note: du04, no scheduler; the #SBATCH lines are comments to a plain bash run. Needs peer access between every pair (checked at startup) and CUDA IPC, so it is a single-node case by construction. MareNostrum 5 would measure the same thing on H100 at the cost of a queue slot.
found_note: this case is why cuda_memcpy carries `ctx_device`. Its first run, before that field existed, produced a PERFECT device-space matrix — rank 0 says 0->1, rank 1 says 1->2, rank 2 2->3, rank 3 3->0, 100 copies of 1 MiB each — and a comm_edges of ONE row: `-1 -> -1`, 400 sends, with link_health.unresolved_device_copy = 400. Nothing in the capture said which rank drove which GPU: mem_object is empty (cudaMalloc is deliberately not hooked), gpu_access needs gpumem which cannot share a process with CUPTI, gpu_kernel is empty (this workload launches no kernels) and there is no NCCL. Neither endpoint of a peer copy can supply it either — one is the rank's, one is not, and the row does not say which. CUPTI reports the issuing CONTEXT's device as a third ordinal on the same record, and that is what closed it.
workload_note: `mpirun -np 4 ipcring 100 1048576`. Rank r opens rank (r+1)%ranks's allocation with cudaIpcOpenMemHandle and issues `iters` cudaMemcpyPeer calls into it, from its own device to the peer's. Every count in the assertions is derived from `ranks`, `iters` and `msg_bytes`; nothing is read off a capture. No CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinning, because cudaMemcpyPeer needs the peer's ordinal to be meaningful in the calling process — which is also the configuration where _device_owner has real work to do.
oracle_note: ring_matrix is the load-bearing assertion and cannot pass vacuously: it builds the expected ring from params with a recursive CTE and LEFT JOINs the capture onto it, so a MISSING edge is an offending row, not an absent one. The suite's usual empty-means-pass shape would go green on a capture with no copies at all.
